## Reuse analytical workflows

An **Analytical Profile** defines which modules run, in what order, and in which report. It helps standardise reporting across monitoring sites and years without duplicating modules. **Profiles select modules; the modules and `camReport` settings define analytical methods and parameters.**

| Profile | Reporting context | REM parameters |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `default` | General ecological reporting | Pooled across years within species |
| `EOW` | European Observatory of Wildlife–oriented workflow | Estimated separately by species and year |

Select a profile suited to your sampling design and analytical objectives. Neither profile guarantees methodological validity or implies formal network endorsement.

## Understand profiles and module pools

Profiles reference modules from two pools: `report` (Ecological Report, `reportSections`) and `status` (Data Status Check, `statusSections`). For example, `report::introduction` and `status::spatial` explicitly identify their source pools; these are **module references**, not R namespace operators.

A profile stores ordered module references and optional parent overrides—not datasets, module code, computed results, or package versions. Applying a profile rebuilds the selected report sections; make any one-off edits **after** applying it.

## 1. Explore available profiles

Create `cm` with `camData()` as shown in [Get Started](https://spatialecology.github.io/camtrapReport/). The examples below illustrate independent operations and are not executed when building this vignette.


```{r inspect-profiles, eval=FALSE}
library(camtrapReport)

profile_names(cm)
section_names(object = cm, profile = "default")
section_names(object = cm, profile = "EOW", report_type = "status")
section_names(object = cm, report_type = "all")
```


Use the [Module Catalog](module-catalog.html) to inspect module requirements. `section_names()` can show both report and status selections.

## 2. Create and apply a profile

Define an ordered selection for each output, register it, and generate the reports:


```{r create-brief-profile, eval=FALSE}
brief <- reportProfile(
  name = "brief",
  description = "A small report for a first inspection",
  report = c("introduction", "methods"),
  status = c("spatial", "temporal", "availability")
)
add_profile(cm, brief)

report(
  cm,
  profile = "brief",
  filename = file.path(tempdir(), "brief-report.html"),
  view = FALSE
)
status(
  cm,
  profile = "brief",
  filename = file.path(tempdir(), "brief-status.html"),
  view = FALSE
)
```


**Order matters:** Parent sections must precede their children (for example, `methods` before `study_area`). Check the hierarchy with `list_Modules()`.

## 3. Change the selected sections

Pass the **complete desired sequence** to `sections()`; ecological and status selections are edited separately.


```{r edit-brief-profile, eval=FALSE}
sections(
  cm,
  n = c("introduction", "methods", "study_area"),
  profile = "brief"
)
sections(cm, profile = "brief")

# The status selection is edited independently:
sections(
  cm,
  n = c("spatial", "availability"),
  profile = "brief",
  report_type = "status"
)
```


Apply a profile before making changes directly to the active report tree; applying it again may replace those changes.

## 4. Combine modules from both pools

A profile can incorporate data-status modules into an ecological report. Explicit `source` and `parent` fields identify their origins and position; the `appendix_eow` module supports this example in both HTML and PDF.


```{r combined-profile, eval=FALSE}
entries <- data.frame(
  source = c("report", "report", "status", "status"),
  module = c("introduction", "appendix_eow", "spatial", "temporal"),
  parent = c(NA, NA, "appendix_eow", "appendix_eow"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
combined <- reportProfile(name = "combined", report = entries)
add_profile(cm, combined)
report(
  cm,
  profile = "combined",
  filename = file.path(tempdir(), "combined-report.html"),
  view = FALSE
)
```


Module names in a rendered selection must be unique, including across pools. Use qualified references or the `source` field when needed.

## 5. Save and share profiles

Export the **current registered profile**, rather than an outdated R variable, then import it into another `camReport` object.


```{r share-brief-profile, eval=FALSE}
profile_file <- tempfile("brief-profile-", fileext = ".yml")
write_profile("brief", profile_file, object = cm)

imported <- read_profile(profile_file)
imported
# For an object with no profile named "brief":
# add_profile(other_cm, imported)
# To deliberately replace the existing profile in cm:
add_profile(cm, imported, overwrite = TRUE)
```


A profile YAML file does **not** contain its modules. Recipients must register any required custom modules separately; see [Module Management](modules.html). Only use modules from trusted sources, as they may execute R code.

## 6. Generate PDF reports

PDF output uses optional `pagedown` and a supported Chrome/Edge browser. Some interactive or HTML-only modules may be excluded according to the registry's `formats` setting.


```{r profile-pdf, eval=FALSE}
report(
  cm,
  profile = "brief",
  filename = file.path(tempdir(), "brief-report-pdf.pdf"),
  view = FALSE
)
```


Check the resulting document and console messages; PDF and HTML may differ in section availability and presentation.

## Troubleshooting and reproducibility

| Issue | Check |
|:--|:--|
| Missing section | Profile selection, module pool, parent hierarchy, and output format |
| Missing figure or estimate | Required data, dependencies, filters, and method assumptions |
| Changes lost after selecting a profile | Apply the profile before editing individual attached sections |
| Imported profile cannot locate a module | Register the referenced module in the receiving object's pool |
| Different PDF and HTML outputs | Module `formats` flags and report messages |

Keep the profile YAML, custom modules, input-data provenance, analytical settings, and package versions together. Review the scientific interpretation of every output: **successful rendering does not establish ecological validity**.

For available analyses, see the [Module Catalog](module-catalog.html). Propose new community workflows through [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/spatialecology/camtrapReport/discussions).
